items.title: Texas 5-star RB commit hits Texas high school football rushing milestone
items.summary:
In Texas' long and storied high school football history, only four players have ever crossed the milestone of more than 10,000 rushing yards.

The number went from four to five Friday night, Nov. 13, as Randle (TX) senior running back and five-star Texas commit Landen Williams-Callis hit the mark with a 9-yard run late in the first quarter of Randle's postseason opener at home against A&M Consolidated.

Williams-Callis entered the postseason needing just 29 yards to hit the mark. 

More: Texas high school football rankings: USA TODAY Sports Super 10 Week 12 

What Williams-Callis has done this season is nothing new for the future Longhorn. 

He broke onto the scene in 2023 as a freshman, rushing for 1,944 yards and 23 touchdowns. He upped the ante his sophomore year, rushing for 2,108 yards and 43 touchdowns as the Lions won the Class 5A Division II championship.

As a junior, Williams-Callis led the Lions to a state championship appearance, rushing for 3,442 yards and 58 touchdowns. Ahead of his senior season on Aug. 1, he announced his commitment to Texas.

While replicating his numbers is something many weren't sure would happen this year, Williams-Callis appears well on his way to setting career bests if the Lions go on a long postseason run. Prior to Friday's game, he was averaging 247.7 yards and nearly four rushing touchdowns per game.

Mount Enterprise (TX) standout Kaegan Ash set the state record last season, completing his high school career with 11,382 yards.

items.title: Jaland Lowe, Vince Ichukwu lead Georgetown to 85-78 win over Clemson
items.summary:
CLEMSON, S.C. (AP) — Jaland Lowe had 21 points and five assists, Vince Iwuchukwu added 18 points on 7-of-9 shooting and grabbed 10 rebounds, and Georgetown blew a 19-point lead before the Hoyas beat Clemson 85-78 on Friday night. 

Elmarko Jackson had 17 points for Georgetown (4-0) and Josiah Parker scored 11. 

Ace Buckner led Clemson with 20 points, Cole Certa scored 14 and Liutauras Lelevicius 10. 

The Hoyas scored 18 consecutive points to take a 16-point lead with 9:34 left in the first half and Jackson's 3-pointer about 3 1/2 minutes later gave Georgetown its biggest lead at 41-22. 

After Lowe made a layup 43 seconds into the second half to push the lead to 15 points, Clemson (3-1) scored 16 of the next 21 to make it 54-50 with 13:18 left in the game.

Certa made layup with 6:23 to play that made gave the Tigers a 66-64 advantage before Jackson score eight points in a 10-1 run and Lowe scored nine points in the final 2:34 to seal it.

Georgetown is 4-0 for the first time since the 2017-18 season when it started 8-0. The Hoyas finished 15-15 that season.

Up next Georgetown: Hosts Navy on Wednesday. 

Clemson: Hosts The Citadel on Monday.

Their flight was taking off about an hour late amid a nationwide grounding of departing flights. "Our original takeoff was 6:35 (p.m.) It's 7:30 now. So it's just an hour late, so can't complain. It could be a lot worse," said Grochowski, 31. "Excited to watch the Lions, so it was worth it."

The Lions and Patriots kick off at 9:30 a.m. EST (3:30 p.m. local time in Munich) on Sunday, Nov. 15.

The French had been waiting 21 years to see their team beat the Springboks at the Stade de France. In that time the team turned through successive generations and multiple iterations, risen, fallen and risen again. Now, at last, they have done it. Only by two, 21-19, and hell, they were hanging on by the fingertips for the final 30 minutes, but they have, at last, beaten the best team in the world in their national stadium. And after all that they did it with a team that had barely won a lineout, lost almost every scrum and which was missing a host of players.

What they did have, however, was Antoine Dupont. No fly-half? No problem. Earlier in the week their head coach, Fabien Galthié, had dismissed the idea that he and his opposite number, Rassie Erasmus, were playing mindgames with each other as “comic-book stuff”. Turns out this was just another bluff. Galthié had said Dupont was going to start at fly-half and, sure, he wore No 10 on his back, but he played the game in his usual position. items.title: Cummins stands firm on ball tampering to leave Australian cricket back where it started | Geoff Lemon
items.summary:
The Test captain kept his promise to answer all questions at a press conference that made his position clear and filled some but not all gaps

Our coverage on Thursday said that Pat Cummins needed to front up, and nobody can fairly say that he didn’t. It was a proper ’til-they-drop affair from Australia’s cricket captain, an hour and eight minutes at a press conference podium taking questions about the 2018 ball-tampering episode until every journalist present ran out of steam. You might have expected some partial concession to teammate Usman Khawaja’s depiction of endemic cheating, but Cummins was firm that this did not reflect the life he’d known. Once more with feeling, but more importantly with detail.

Media accounts will now depict this as Cummins and Khawaja at war, because a falling-out among friends is a juicy story to fatten up and serve for gluttony. It isn’t fair, because both have emphasised the importance of their friendship, strained as it must now be. As two thoughtful people with shared history, they have a better chance than most to find a way through.

items.title: NFL quarterbacks are under more pressure than ever from rushers. Why?

Despite all the advantages offenses have secured over the years, defenses are better at pressuring the QB than any other time in recent history

The Baltimore Ravens are preparing to start their fourth quarterback this year, Jacoby Brissett, against the beleaguered Los Angeles Chargers on Monday, because of injuries to Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley and Joe Fagnano. That puts them dangerously close to the NFL record of five within a single season (a record shared by the 1984 Bears and 2023 Browns when excluding the 1987 strike season).

Jackson, Huntley and Fagnano were all injured after taking hits in games. And if it seems like quarterbacks are taking punishment more often this year, your eyes aren’t deceiving you. Through nine weeks, quarterbacks have been hit on 15.1% of their dropbacks, the most we’ve seen since 2006, when hits were first logged in official box scores.

items.title: The beautiful game: revived art prize gives football its creative due once more | Emma John
items.summary:
Football and the art world have long remained distant but the breadth of entries for this year’s award reveals a healthy revival

It may be the Beautiful Game, but in its early decades football was a rare subject for artists. The Italian Futurist Umberto Boccioni whirled an athlete’s body into a vortex of movement in his 1913 painting Dynamism of a Soccer Player. You can see one of the earliest fine art depictions of a match – a smoggy, factory-adjactent scene called Any Wintry Afternoon in England – at the Manchester Art Gallery. If 1930s abstraction is more your thing, you can enjoy decoding the geometric shapes in Kazimir Malevich’s Painterly Realism of a Football Player – Color Masses in the 4th Dimension. I’m guessing the small green pea shape is a ball.

These, in any case, were exceptions. In 1953 the Football Association launched an art prize, backed by the newly formed Arts Council: the winning works included Going To The Match by LS Lowry, with its crowds flocking to Bolton Wanderers’ then home ground, Burnden Park. An exhibition of the submissions, Football and The Fine Arts, toured the country and the FA secretary, Sir Stanley Rous, said he hoped it would finally break the barrier between those two worlds.
